text:
maya: customer-ops wants a fast way to route a single org to their dedicated pool for contract-driven incidents. can we add a console action + API?
ajay: yes but needs strict audit, TTLs, and telemetry. otherwise danger.
kevin: propose an "ephemeral bypass" object: immutable for a minute after create, includes created_by, expires_at, reason, target_pool, audit_id. logged and non-escalating by default.
sasha: router precedence question: does ephemeral bypass trump sticky pins and header overrides? we should define an explicit eval order.
maya: sales wants 1-click UI with TTL presets (1h/4h/8h/24h), reason input, and a parallel API for programmatic use.
kevin: sample API POST: 
```
POST /api/v1/routing/ephemeral_overrides
{
  "org_id":"org_abc",
  "kind":"ephemeral_bypass",
  "target":"dedicated:pool-eu-2",
  "created_by":"maya",
  "expires_at":"2026-06-01T12:00:00Z",
  "reason":"contractual failover",
  "audit_id":"uuid-1234"
}
```
ajay: server-side validation must check target model compatibility (tokenizer, seq_len) and region entitlements. also capture a route_snapshot id for audits.
rachel: UI idea: small card "Active Ephemeral Overrides" with count + table (org, target, expires_at, created_by, reason) and actions (revoke, extend). include a checkbox "invalidate per-org caches on apply" (opt-in).
sasha: safety: bypass should be applied at router decision layer before header parsing so X-Redwood-Route can't defeat it. allow an internal debug override flag for SRE testing.
kevin: security: creation limited to admin/support-manager roles. support agents can submit a request that auto-approves with manager sign-off within 15 minutes. all actions HMAC-signed when via API: header e.g. `X-Rdwd-Bypass: org:expires:signature`. sign keys per-region via KMS.
ajay: rate-limits/alerts: if same org creates/extends >3 times in 24h, emit alert and require manual approval. also alert product-ops when concurrent active bypasses > 10.
sasha: cache corner-case: switching pools with different tokenizer or KV prefixes can corrupt state. router must call cache-flush hook during switch unless preserve-caches checked. document for runbook.
rachel: telemetry events: ephemeral_bypass.created, .extended, .revoked, .expired, .approval.requested. include org_id, created_by, ttl_seconds, target, audit_id, route_snapshot_id. store route snapshot in audit store and reference by id.
kevin: tests: unit tests for eval precedence, integration e2e with header/sticky permutations, chaos test where dedicated pool is unhealthy and bypass must fallback cleanly. add TTL expiry test to verify expired events and cache clearing.
maya: rollout: behind feature-flag in internal console -> small beta with 2 customers -> GA with 180d audit retention. docs and runbook before beta.
ajay: I'll draft the RFC (payloads, HMAC scheme, metric names, snapshot format). aim EOD tomorrow.
kevin: I'll implement router changes + cache flush hook, plus test matrix.
sasha: I'll own runbook + revoke CLI snippets. sample revoke: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" /api/v1/routing/ephemeral_overrides/:id/revoke
```
rachel: I'll mock dashboard widgets and alerts in observability board.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/ephemeral-bypass-api -> staging 2026-03-25T14:00:00Z :rocket:
maya: one more: make sure TTL auto-extension is tracked and surfaced in audit (prevent silent endless renewals). if same actor extends >3x, require manager approval.
ajay: good call; include extension_count in telemetry and a discrete audit event per extension.
kevin: also forbid cross-region target unless org has cross-region entitlement claim. validate server-side.
sasha: postmortem hook: if bypass involved in incident, link route_snapshot_id to incident ticket for easier replay.
maya: thanks team. RFC owners please ping when ready; demo UI in next ops sync. :eyes:
